notes: Matches the reference: unquoted-brace checks are applied consistently across the dispenser and parser through clean Token helper methods, with good dispenser and parse tests; it misses two smaller reference tweaks, the quoted '{}' fall-through to the newline/nesting break and the quoted address suffix check.

Matches the reference: unquoted-brace checks via Token methods cover the dispenser, directive, import, blockTokens and open/close helpers, with solid dispenser and parser tests; it misses two of the reference's extra fixes (the quoted 'addr{' suffix check in addresses() and gating the quoted '{}' branch in directive()), but these are minor edge cases.

Slugs are applied recursively up the branch ancestry, so sections, nested sections, taxonomies, terms, regular pages and leaf-bundle resources all get the slugged directory, and paths without any slug are left unchanged; it keeps both `Section` and an override `Dir` in the descriptor, which is a little less clean than the reference's single `Dir`, and `path.Join` normalizes unusual slugs slightly differently, but the test covers the scenarios well.

Recursively applies ancestor section, taxonomy and term slugs through a new optional Dir field that is only set when a slug applies, so unslugged paths keep their old behavior; it covers branch pages, leaf pages, non-section intermediate dirs and bundle resources, and the integration test is thorough, though it is slightly less unified than the reference (keeps Section and falls back to it) and does not test DisablePathToLower.

Applies the transform after consolidation, preserving exec, env, tags and options, rejecting multiple scenarios and the main CLI shortcut flags, with good unit and integration tests. It misses two edge cases the reference handles: execution-segment flags are not rejected, and shortcuts set in lower layers (e.g. K6_ITERATIONS or K6_DURATION from the environment) still wipe the script's scenario before --once runs, so the default function runs instead of the scenario's exec.

C1 adds `--once` to the shared option flagset and rewrites the consolidated scenarios into a 1-VU/1-iteration `shared-iterations` executor that keeps exec, env, tags and options, and it rejects multiple scenarios and the vus/iterations/duration/stage flags. It misses that a lower layer's shortcuts (for example `K6_DURATION`/`K6_ITERATIONS` in the environment, or the config file) wipe scripted scenarios during consolidation, before `--once` ever sees them. It also neither rejects nor drops `--execution-segment`, and it drops shortcuts silently without a warning, but it ships thorough unit, integration and archive tests.

Uses the same approach as the reference: a bare literal in parens is lifted into a Wrapped unary-plus DurationExpr, and Pretty is fixed to match. It also adds durationLiteralValue so parse-time checks keep working for wrapped literals (positive range, division/modulo by zero), e.g. `foo[(0)]` and `5/(0)`. Minor nits: the extra ExperimentalDurationExpr guard in applyUnaryOpToDurationExpr is unexplained, and StartPos excludes the opening paren. Tests are thorough across parse AST, error cases, printer and prettier.

Fixes the bug the same way as the reference: a parenthesised number literal is lifted into a Wrapped unary-plus DurationExpr, and Pretty is updated to match. It also adds a durationLiteralValue helper so the parse-time positivity and division/modulo-by-zero checks still fire on `(0)` and `-(5)`; this goes beyond the reference but prevents a real regression, and these cases are well tested. Minor oddities: wrapping in applyUnaryOpToDurationExpr is gated on the experimental flag, and positions exclude the parens.

This fixes the reported single-module for_each/count case by keeping every same-module block, but it still deduplicates at the ConfigResource level across modules. A parent import of one instance (e.g. `module.child.test_object.b[0]`) therefore silently discards the child's blocks for other instances (`b[1]`), which is the same silent-drop bug this issue reports. The reference avoids this by deduplicating per resource instance after expansion, and the candidate's own unit test asserts the incorrect drop.

Fixes the reported same-module case by returning all import blocks, but parent-over-child overrides still happen per config resource rather than per instance, so a child module's imports for other instances are still dropped silently whenever a parent imports any one instance (the candidate's own test locks this in), which likely explains the 1/3 hidden pass rate.

Follows the issue's sentinel-error design and early return works in partials, regular templates and `try`, but it has real gaps: a pipeline like `{{ return x | string }}` silently drops the rest of the pipeline instead of erroring, and it weakens the existing regression test's assertion to hide this. It also silently ignores `return <value>` in non-partial templates and swallows valued returns inside nested `template` actions. Scope is too wide: it changes the `ExecuteWithContextAndKey` signature and edits docs, and the package suite fails.

Early return now works from any template position via a ReturnError sentinel trapped at template boundaries, but several cases go wrong: `return x | string` silently drops the rest of the pipeline instead of being rejected, value-returns in non-partials and inside `template` calls are swallowed, and `$v | return` in a partial falls back to rendered output; the patch also changes the ExecuteWithContextAndKey signature, edits docs, and rewrites an existing test assertion to match its own behaviour (likely the failing hidden test).
